A THOUGHTFUL LITTLE MATCH

Find your next move.

Predict opponent occupancy, intentionally push or block a planned step, program orientation that compensates conveyor rotation, reserve needed command for next draw. A good solo route can fail because other robot moves first.

Take a seat
How to play
7×7 factory with pits, conveyors and rotators, two robots and three ordered checkpoints. Each round both receive five command cards from own identical cyclic deck (Forward1, Forward2, Back1, Left, Right, Wait), select three and order into registers. Each register lower printed priority robot moves first; forward can push opponent if next cell free, otherwise stops. Then all conveyors move simultaneously and rotators turn occupied robots. Finish entire three-register cycle, discard used and redraw. Opponent commits before human program reveal; checkpoints count only on robot movement/conveyor settling, pits reset robot to last checkpoint and lose one of three lives. Conveyor resolution is fixed: compute every robot conveyor destination from its post-command square; if two destinations coincide both stay; if a target is occupied by a robot that is not vacating, mover stays; swaps between vacating robots are allowed. Conveyor movement never pushes. Arrival on pit removes robot before rotators resolve; new checkpoint respawn occurs after register and cannot push another robot (occupied respawn waits offboard until free).
Visit all three checkpoints and exit before rival wins; lose if own lives zero or rival finishes. Simultaneous finish ties.
The compact race ends in a draw after 24 programs. The exact course is D4→B2→F2→D1; D4 also rotates robots clockwise after every register.

Each round both receive five command cards from own identical cyclic deck (Forward1, Forward2, Back1, Left, Right, Wait), select three and order into registers. Finish entire three-register cycle, discard used and redraw. Opponent commits before human program reveal; checkpoints count only on robot movement/conveyor settling, pits reset robot to last checkpoint and lose one of three lives. Conveyor resolution is fixed: compute every robot conveyor destination from its post-command square; if two destinations coincide both stay; if a target is occupied by a robot that is not vacating, mover stays; swaps between vacating robots are allowed. Conveyor movement never pushes. Arrival on pit removes robot before rotators resolve; new checkpoint respawn occurs after register and cannot push another robot (occupied respawn waits offboard until free).
Visit all three checkpoints and exit before rival wins; lose if own lives zero or rival finishes. Simultaneous finish ties.
The compact race ends in a draw after 24 programs. The exact course is D4→B2→F2→D1; D4 also rotates robots clockwise after every register.

How to play
7×7 factory with pits, conveyors and rotators, two robots and three ordered checkpoints. Each round both receive five command cards from own identical cyclic deck (Forward1, Forward2, Back1, Left, Right, Wait), select three and order into registers. Each register lower printed priority robot moves first; forward can push opponent if next cell free, otherwise stops. Then all conveyors move simultaneously and rotators turn occupied robots. Finish entire three-register cycle, discard used and redraw. Opponent commits before human program reveal; checkpoints count only on robot movement/conveyor settling, pits reset robot to last checkpoint and lose one of three lives. Conveyor resolution is fixed: compute every robot conveyor destination from its post-command square; if two destinations coincide both stay; if a target is occupied by a robot that is not vacating, mover stays; swaps between vacating robots are allowed. Conveyor movement never pushes. Arrival on pit removes robot before rotators resolve; new checkpoint respawn occurs after register and cannot push another robot (occupied respawn waits offboard until free).
Visit all three checkpoints and exit before rival wins; lose if own lives zero or rival finishes. Simultaneous finish ties.
The compact race ends in a draw after 24 programs. The exact course is D4→B2→F2→D1; D4 also rotates robots clockwise after every register.

How to play
7×7 factory with pits, conveyors and rotators, two robots and three ordered checkpoints. Each round both receive five command cards from own identical cyclic deck (Forward1, Forward2, Back1, Left, Right, Wait), select three and order into registers. Each register lower printed priority robot moves first; forward can push opponent if next cell free, otherwise stops. Then all conveyors move simultaneously and rotators turn occupied robots. Finish entire three-register cycle, discard used and redraw. Opponent commits before human program reveal; checkpoints count only on robot movement/conveyor settling, pits reset robot to last checkpoint and lose one of three lives. Conveyor resolution is fixed: compute every robot conveyor destination from its post-command square; if two destinations coincide both stay; if a target is occupied by a robot that is not vacating, mover stays; swaps between vacating robots are allowed. Conveyor movement never pushes. Arrival on pit removes robot before rotators resolve; new checkpoint respawn occurs after register and cannot push another robot (occupied respawn waits offboard until free).
Visit all three checkpoints and exit before rival wins; lose if own lives zero or rival finishes. Simultaneous finish ties.
The compact race ends in a draw after 24 programs. The exact course is D4→B2→F2→D1; D4 also rotates robots clockwise after every register.

Finish entire three-register cycle, discard used and redraw. Opponent commits before human program reveal; checkpoints count only on robot movement/conveyor settling, pits reset robot to last checkpoint and lose one of three lives. Conveyor movement never pushes. Arrival on pit removes robot before rotators resolve; new checkpoint respawn occurs after register and cannot push another robot (occupied respawn waits offboard until free).
Visit all three checkpoints and exit before rival wins; lose if own lives zero or rival finishes. Simultaneous finish ties.

Each round both receive five command cards from own identical cyclic deck (Forward1, Forward2, Back1, Left, Right, Wait), select three and order into registers. Each register lower printed priority robot moves first; forward can push opponent if next cell free, otherwise stops. Then all conveyors move simultaneously and rotators turn occupied robots. Finish entire three-register cycle, discard used and redraw. Opponent commits before human program reveal; checkpoints count only on robot movement/conveyor settling, pits reset robot to last checkpoint and lose one of three lives. Conveyor resolution is fixed: compute every robot conveyor destination from its post-command square; if two destinations coincide both stay; if a target is occupied by a robot that is not vacating, mover stays; swaps between vacating robots are allowed. Conveyor movement never pushes. Arrival on pit removes robot before rotators resolve; new checkpoint respawn occurs after register and cannot push another robot (occupied respawn waits offboard until free).
Visit all three checkpoints and exit before rival wins; lose if own lives zero or rival finishes. Simultaneous finish ties.
The compact race ends in a draw after 24 programs. The exact course is D4→B2→F2→D1; D4 also rotates robots clockwise after every register.

How to play
7×7 factory with pits, conveyors and rotators, two robots and three ordered checkpoints. Each round both receive five command cards from own identical cyclic deck (Forward1, Forward2, Back1, Left, Right, Wait), select three and order into registers. Conveyor movement never pushes. Arrival on pit removes robot before rotators resolve; new checkpoint respawn occurs after register and cannot push another robot (occupied respawn waits offboard until free).
Visit all three checkpoints and exit before rival wins; lose if own lives zero or rival finishes. Simultaneous finish ties.
The compact race ends in a draw after 24 programs. The exact course is D4→B2→F2→D1; D4 also rotates robots clockwise after every register.

Each round both receive five command cards from own identical cyclic deck (Forward1, Forward2, Back1, Left, Right, Wait), select three and order into registers. Arrival on pit removes robot before rotators resolve; new checkpoint respawn occurs after register and cannot push another robot (occupied respawn waits offboard until free).

How to play
7×7 factory with pits, conveyors and rotators, two robots and three ordered checkpoints. Each round both receive five command cards from own identical cyclic deck (Forward1, Forward2, Back1, Left, Right, Wait), select three and order into registers. Each register lower printed priority robot moves first; forward can push opponent if next cell free, otherwise stops. Then all conveyors move simultaneously and rotators turn occupied robots. Finish entire three-register cycle, discard used and redraw. Opponent commits before human program reveal; checkpoints count only on robot movement/conveyor settling, pits reset robot to last checkpoint and lose one of three lives. Conveyor resolution is fixed: compute every robot conveyor destination from its post-command square; if two destinations coincide both stay; if a target is occupied by a robot that is not vacating, mover stays; swaps between vacating robots are allowed. Conveyor movement never pushes. Arrival on pit removes robot before rotators resolve; new checkpoint respawn occurs after register and cannot push another robot (occupied respawn waits offboard until free).
Visit all three checkpoints and exit before rival wins; lose if own lives zero or rival finishes. Simultaneous finish ties.
The compact race ends in a draw after 24 programs. The exact course is D4→B2→F2→D1; D4 also rotates robots clockwise after every register.
